newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: D&B keeps Slovenia credit rating steady at DB3a.
newsitem.headline: D&B keeps Slovenia credit rating steady at DB3a.

text.p: Slovenia's credit rating will stay at DB3a for February although the country has not yet elected a new government, credit rating agency Dun and Bradstreet's Ljubljana representative said on Thursday.

"The political situation remained somewhat fluid in Slovenia in January, but this has done little to undermine the country's stable overall risk environment," the agency said in its latest Risk & Payment Review.
On Thursday, Slovenia's parliament began to debate approval of the new cabinet of prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats.
The vote was expected to take place later in the day, almost three months after an inconclusive November 10 general election.
D&B awarded Slovenia a DB3a rating for the eighth successive month, placing it behind the Czech Republic and in front of Poland.
The agency warned Slovenia's relations with other successor republics of the former Yugoslavia could potentially pose a problem in the short and medium-term.

"While Croatia in January 1997 signed a U.S.-led initiative to improve cooperation in South and East Europe, Slovenia retains reservations over this agreement and would prefer to operate within the European Union context," the agency said.
Slovenia, which signed an association agreement with the EU in June 1996, hopes to become a member by the year 2001. The country gained independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991.
The agency also pointed out that Slovenia's imports continued to grow while exports were on the downtrend.

According to the Bank of Slovenia, the country's trade deficit rose to $192 million in November from a deficit of $82 million in October and a shortfall of $124 million a year ago. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana Newsroom, 386-61-126-3644
